# Results — Study 413 (Bull Flag)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a bull flag
(sharp flagpole + brief shallow flag) breaks upward and resumes the prior uptrend** — tested with
the closest **mechanical** definition of the figure on daily OHLC: a steep run-up over a short
window (the flagpole), a tight flat-to-down consolidation that gives back only a fraction of the
pole (the flag), and a confirmed close back above the flag's high (the breakout), across **SPY +
29 US large-caps**. We measure the forward return after each confirmed breakout as an **excess
over each name's own base rate** (does the figure beat buy-and-hold for that name?), with a
one-sample/HAC *t*, a **same-tape label-shuffle placebo**, a **down-break symmetry** myth-check,
and a synthetic positive control. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

> **Chart figures are partly subjective.** The bull flag is in the eye of the beholder. We do
> **not** claim to capture every flag a human would draw — we test one transparent, reproducible
> mechanical definition and say so. A different rule set would find a different (overlapping) event
> set; the qualitative verdict is what travels.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **auto-adjusted** (split + dividend) OHLC — 30 long-listed US large-caps incl. SPY (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-05-31** (last full bar **2026-05-29**; no partial month) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**21.4** years; 5,385 daily bars) |
| Fingerprint | `2d8d0fde0371` (sha1[:12] of the close panel) |
| Detector | steep flagpole (≥12% over 12 bars) + tight flat-to-down flag (≤50% pole retrace, ≤10% range, not net-up) + first close clearing the flag high |
| Events | **638** confirmed bull-flag **up**-breaks (SPY alone: **4**); **531** down-breaks (myth check) |
| Timing / costs | enter the close **1 day after** the breakout (no look-ahead); hold 5/10/20/40 days; **5 bps** one-way × 2 = 10 bps round trip |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names *still trading* in 2026. A
> fixed surviving-names panel cannot include firms that delisted after a failed breakout, which
> tilts post-breakout forward returns mildly **up** — i.e. the bias works *for* the figure, and the
> figure still comes out **negative**. Total-return adjusted closes (we label them as such).

## The signal — forward return after a confirmed up-break, EXCESS over the base rate

The excess subtracts each name's own unconditional mean forward return, so the test is **"does the
figure beat buy-and-hold for that name?"** — not "is the market up." The **placebo p** is the share
of 5,000 draws of *random entry dates on the same tape* (same count) whose excess **beats** the
observed one.

| horizon | n events | excess mean | raw mean | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 634 | −0.19% | +0.14% | 47% | −1.07 | −1.12 | 0.60 | −0.29% |
| 10-day | 634 | −0.32% | +0.34% | 47% | −1.23 | −1.31 | 0.61 | −0.42% |
| 20-day | 628 | −0.38% | +0.94% | 49% | −1.07 | −1.07 | 0.59 | −0.48% |
| 40-day | 624 | −0.60% | +2.00% | 50% | −1.21 | −1.10 | 0.60 | −0.70% |

Read it carefully — this is the whole study. After a *confirmed* bull-flag breakout the stock's
forward return is **positive in raw terms** (+0.14% to +2.00%, because these names drift up
anyway) but **negative as an excess over its own base rate at every horizon** (−0.19% to −0.60%,
*t* ≈ −1.1, win-rate **below 50%**). The figure does **worse** than simply holding the name. The
same-tape **placebo p sits at ~0.60**: a random set of entry dates on the same names beats the
breakout about **three times in five**. There is no positive edge to begin with — the naive *t* is
*negative*, so this never even reaches the "real number, wrong attribution" stage that snared the
ascending triangle. The bull-flag breakout is, if anything, a mild **drag**.

## Costs — irrelevant, because the gross edge is already negative

A round trip is **5 bps one-way × 2 = 10 bps**. Net columns above. There is nothing to erode: the
gross excess is already below zero, so costs only deepen a loss that was never an edge.

## Myth check — does the flag resolve UP far more than DOWN? (the symmetry test)

The cleanest within-study control. Run the **identical** detector but require a break *below* the
flag's low (the resolution a chartist would call **bearish / failed flag**). If the figure
genuinely *chooses* the upward direction, the down-break excess should be **clearly negative**, well
under the up-break.

| horizon | n | down-break excess | raw | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 529 | +0.71% | +1.05% | +3.88 | 0.22 |
| 10-day | 527 | +0.56% | +1.22% | +1.99 | 0.33 |
| 20-day | 525 | +0.68% | +1.99% | +1.67 | 0.35 |
| 40-day | 523 | +0.94% | +3.51% | +1.60 | 0.35 |

The punchline is brutal for the folklore. The **down**-break — the "failed flag," the resolution a
chartist would call bearish — drifts **up MORE** than the textbook up-break at every horizon
(+0.71% vs −0.19% at 5 days; +0.68% vs −0.38% at 20 days). The flag's *resolution direction* carries
no upward information; if anything the "wrong" direction does better. (Neither clears the same-tape
placebo, *p* = 0.22–0.35 — so even the down-break "edge" is the names' own drift, not the figure.)
A pattern whose entire premise is *direction* cannot have its two resolutions point the same way.
"It breaks upward and resumes the trend" is the part that's **busted**.

## Robustness — strictness doesn't rescue it

| min pole / max retrace | n events | excess (20d) | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ≥10% / ≤60% (loose) | 1,071 | −0.66% | −2.64 | 0.71 |
| **≥12% / ≤50% (headline)** | **628** | **−0.38%** | **−1.07** | **0.59** |
| ≥16% / ≤40% (strict) | 235 | +0.38% | +0.57 | 0.44 |

Tightening the detector shrinks the loss toward zero (the strict setting limps to +0.38% on just
235 events at *t* = 0.57) but **never produces a placebo-clean positive**: *p* stays at
0.44–0.71 everywhere. No definition of "a cleaner flag" turns the figure into an edge — the
invariance is the signature of *no signal*, not a tuning problem.

## Myth check — does it beat SPY buy-and-hold? (the README hook)

The hook asks specifically about **SPY**. The detector finds only **4** clean bull flags on the SPY
tape in 21 years — far too few to certify anything:

| horizon | n | excess vs SPY hold | raw | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 4 | +0.12% | +0.35% | +0.05 | 0.48 |
| 10-day | 4 | −2.12% | −1.65% | −0.50 | 0.91 |
| 20-day | 4 | +1.45% | +2.39% | +0.35 | 0.25 |
| 40-day | 4 | +0.98% | +2.83% | +0.12 | 0.40 |

With *n* = 4 and *t* ≈ 0 the SPY-only version is uncertifiable noise, and the broad-basket symmetry
test already showed the breakout direction is uninformative. The figure does **not** demonstrably
beat SPY buy-and-hold.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful (and the placebo is the right arbiter)

On a deterministic panel where we **plant** clean bull flags and a *known* post-breakout drift, the
detector + inference behave exactly as they must — proving the negative real-tape result is a true
absence of edge, not a broken pipeline:

| planted edge | planted | detected | n | excess (20d) | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 160 | 218 | 218 | −0.88% | −2.61 | 0.66 | 39% |
| **+0.20** (large planted drift) | 160 | 384 | 384 | +5.63% | **+16.43** | **0.001** | 80% |

With **no** planted continuation the inference does not manufacture a positive (excess −0.88%,
placebo *p* = 0.66 — well inside the noise). Plant a real +20% continuation and everything lights
up (excess +5.63%, *t* = 16.43, placebo *p* = 0.001, win 80%). The engine *can* bank a true edge —
it simply finds none on the real tape, where the bull-flag breakout is even slightly *negative*.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The up-break excess-over-base-rate is **negative at every horizon** (−0.38% at
  20 days, one-sample *t* = −1.07, HAC *t* = −1.07), the win-rate is **below 50%**, and the same-tape
  **placebo p ≈ 0.60** (random dates win ~3-in-5). The strictness sweep never produces a
  placebo-clean positive, and a zero-edge synthetic control correctly stays inside the noise while a
  planted edge lights up at *t* = 16.4. Survivorship tilts the test *for* the figure and it still
  comes out negative. There is no signal to certify.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is nothing to deploy: the gross excess is below zero before any
  cost, costs only deepen the loss (net −0.29% to −0.70%), and the SPY-only version rests on **4**
  events at *t* ≈ 0. Buying the bull-flag breakout slightly *underperforms* just holding the name.
- **"Resolves up specifically"? — BUSTED.** The pattern's entire premise is *direction*, and the
  direction carries **negative** information here: the **down**-break of the identical flag drifts
  **up more** than the up-break at every horizon (+0.71% vs −0.19% at 5 days; +0.68% vs −0.38% at 20
  days). Break up or break down, the stock drifts the same — the post-figure return is a property of
  the **names**, not the **break direction**. The bull flag is a momentum tell dressed as a
  directional breakout signal — and a poorly calibrated one.
